title: Customer-facing regression triage and graceful degradation protocol
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: This ticket defines an operational playbook, automation, and short-term fixes for customer-facing regressions discovered during model rollouts across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The goal is to standardize triage, choose safe mitigation (graceful degradation vs immediate rollback), coordinate KV cache and inference state reconciliation, and publish customer-facing comms. This work covers: sentinel-trigger detection, automated route shifting, quick model-variant downgrade, tenant-scoped throttling, and a lightweight live-patch path for edge fixes. The output will be a runnable runbook, 2 automation scripts (traffic-slicer and variant-guard), and a kit of email/console templates for SRE/Support to use.
acceptance_criteria: A clear decision matrix that maps observed regression signals to actions (degrade, downgrade, rollback, patch)
Traffic-slicer automation that can shift 100% of affected tenant traffic to a safe variant within 3 minutes
KV cache reconciliation checklist documented and validated on a staging tenant
Communication templates for customer-facing and internal messages reviewed by Support and PM
Runbook tested in a simulated canary failure and documented results in Confluence
tasks: Finalize triage decision matrix and get PM sign-off
Implement traffic-slicer orchestration (github PR) and add telemetry hooks
Write KV cache reconciliation checklist and automations to flush or sync per-tenant caches
Create customer communication templates and run tabletop with Support
Run two simulated canary failure drills (hosted + dedicated) and capture results
Ship minimal runbook and automation to runtime-1.24 canary cluster
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting with PM, SRE, Support. Aligned on goals and scope. Decided to prioritize automation for traffic-slicer before live-patch tooling.
2026-03-11: Drafted triage decision matrix; initial ruleset available in Confluence (see links). Need PM review on SLA thresholds.
2026-03-12: Implemented PoC traffic-slicer orchestration — routes by tenant ID and model-variant compatibility. PoC ran on internal canary cluster with synthetic load (results attached).

2026-03-13: Variant-guard design reviewed by runtime team. Trade-off: immediate downgrade reduces correctness but maintains availability; live-patch is higher risk and requires additional safety checks. Agreed to prefer downgrade for P0 regressions unless data-sensitivity prevents downgrade in private deployments.
2026-03-14: Opened PR for traffic-slicer controlplane hooks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4583. Started tabletop with Support; updated communication templates per feedback.
rollback_steps: Step 1: Evaluate signals (baseline latency, token error rate, customer error reports). If deviation > configured SLAs proceed to Step 2.
Step 2: Attempt variant-guard downgrade for affected tenant slice (shift traffic to vetted non-regressing variant). Monitor for 5 minutes.
Step 3: If downgrade fails to restore quality, invoke traffic-slicer to isolate tenant(s) and shift to dedicated fallback pool or previous model version.

Step 4: If fallback pool capacity unavailable or private deployment constraints block fallback, perform coordinated rollback per deployment type (hosted: automated rollback; dedicated/private: notify oncall and begin manual rollback procedure).
Step 5: Run KV cache reconciliation script to invalidate incompatible prefixes and warm cache with safe prompts if necessary.
Step 6: Reconcile billing/metrics and notify customers after fix. Create follow-up tickets for permanent remedy.
communications_template: Short internal notification: 'ALERT: Canary regression detected for model {model_id} in {region}. Initial mitigation: {action_taken}. Impact: {tenants_impacted}. Next steps: SRE oncall and runtime engineers to investigate. Customer-facing template (support): 'We detected an issue impacting your model responses and have shifted traffic to a safe variant to maintain service. Our engineers are actively investigating and will provide updates every 30 minutes.'
postmortem_plan: If this playbook is invoked for a P0 incident: capture timeline, root cause analysis, whether variant-guard or rollback was used, KV cache state, rollout config that triggered regression, and customer impact. Publish within 72 hours and include DB of lessons learned mapped to the decision matrix for improvement.
notes: Trade-offs captured: 1) Downgrade reduces feature/regression exposure quickly but may change output semantics; 2) Live-patch is preferred only for small deterministic tokenizer or tokenization mapping bugs; 3) Private deployments may require customer approval for variant downgrades — include pre-approved emergency clauses in contracts where possible.
next_steps: Finish PR review for traffic-slicer, complete tabletop with Support and Legal for private deployment fallback approvals, schedule two drills (hosted and dedicated) before 2026-03-21, and merge runbook into on-call playbooks.
